newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU SCORES PART VICTORY OVER INQUIRY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU SCORES PART VICTORY OVER INQUIRY.

text.p: The embattled South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) claimed a victory in their fight against allegations ranging from financial mismanagement to racism following a meeting with Sports Minister Steve Tshwete in Pretoria on Friday.
SARFU said the three-man team set up to investigate the charges will not now contain a member of the National Olympic Committee of South Africa (NOCSA) -- one of the sticking points for SARFU.

However SARFU have not been given a copy of the allegedly incriminating dossier compiled by former Transvaal vice-president Brian van Rooyen. SARFU confirmed they will apply to the Supreme Court for its release.
"The meeting was extrememly positive and we are pleased with the outcome," SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer told reporters.
"We will further assist the ministry in every possible way to bring this matter to a speedy conclusion."

SARFU had threatened not to attend the meeting with Tshwete if a member of NOCSA was placed on the team claiming that it would be unfair to rugby's commercial partners to have contracts divulged to other sports.
In response Tshwete let it be known that a commission of inquiry would be appointed if SARFU failed to attend.
The investigations team will be led by the director general of the sport and recreation ministry, Mthobi Tyamzashe.
